lesson.title: 911 – Procedure 104: Final Dispositions (90–99 Series)
objectives: Explain when final dispositions may be entered on an event.
Use 10-90 disposition expansions (F1, F2, J1, J2, N, N3) correctly.
Differentiate between UNFOUNDED, UNNECESSARY, and GONE ON ARRIVAL outcomes.
Apply 10-91 NON-CRIME CONDITION CORRECTED and related home visit codes.

questions.stem: According to Procedure 104, when should a final disposition be entered for an assignment?

choices.text: As soon as the unit arrives on the scene.
After the unit finishes all work related to the assignment, including paperwork, forms, and notifications, and is available for another assignment.
Any time the dispatcher believes the call is probably over.
As soon as the caller hangs up.

questions.solution: Procedure 104 states that final dispositions are to be input only when a unit is completely finished with the assignment and available for another assignment.

questions.stem: A crime in progress is reported, but the responding unit finds only a minor dispute which they correct. No crime occurred. Which final disposition BEST matches the example in Procedure 104?
questions.solution: The guide explicitly gives this as an example where 10-91 should be used; it is not an unfounded call.

questions.stem: A 10-91 Non-crime condition corrected should be treated the same as an unfounded call.
Code 10-90 F1 is used when a Domestic Incident Report (DIR) is prepared but no offense is alleged.
10-90 F2 is DOMESTIC INCIDENT REPORT (DIR PREPARED) __________ INCIDENT, while 10-90 J2 is DOMESTIC INCIDENT REPORT (DIR PREPARED) __________ for child abuse cases.
Code 10-90 N3 is NOTICE/DEFERRED SERVICE – UNFOUNDED OR UNNECESSARY ALARM, used when service of a notice is to be made at a later time when the premise is __________.
Match each 10-90 disposition expansion with its description.
answer: DOMESTIC INCIDENT REPORT (DIR PREPARED) – NO OFFENSE ALLEGED.
DOMESTIC INCIDENT REPORT (DIR PREPARED) – UNFOUNDED INCIDENT.
DOMESTIC INCIDENT REPORT (DIR PREPARED) – NO OFFENSE (Child Abuse DIR).
DOMESTIC INCIDENT REPORT (DIR PREPARED) – UNFOUNDED (Child Abuse DIR).
NOTICE SERVED – UNFOUNDED OR UNNECESSARY ALARM.
NOTICE/DEFERRED SERVICE – UNFOUNDED OR UNNECESSARY ALARM (service later when premise is open).

questions.stem: Match each disposition letter from the final dispositions section with its meaning.
answer: U
UNABLE TO GAIN ENTRY – unknown if event occurred because entry could not be made.
V2
UNSUCCESSFUL VISIT – used to track Domestic Violence Officer home visits.
X
UNFOUNDED – incident reported (or related incident) never happened; report is untrue.
Y
UNNECESSARY – incident did occur, but police response was not necessary.
Z
GONE ON ARRIVAL – incident did occur, but parties left before police arrived.
I1–I5
LEP FINALS (Domestic Incidents only): Language Line, Certified MOS, bilingual public, or no interpretation necessary.
HOME VISIT/NON-CRIME used to track domestic violence home visits and document DV data.
